svg.text: weathered grey rock, mauve heather and russet bracken, wind-bent trees, stacked granite tors; the rocky highland (not volcanic)
A. At fight distance, noon: the ground profile, the cover silhouettes, the far land as a value ladder. The two grey figures are 75 units tall (a fighter): scale only, no character art.
Palette at noon (the world-light tint per sky key multiplies it; lit, mid and shade are the three faces of one surface; the far ladder is each ridge hazed toward the horizon)

Readability (docs/art/dynamic-sky.md section 6): worst aura against any tone 21.5 CIEDE2000 (rule: 20 or more), worst Protagonist or rival body against ground, rock or vegetation 17.4 (rule: 15 or more), over every sky key with the world-light tint.
B. What the fight leaves: scorched (a beam along the ground), cratered (an impact), burned (fire on what grows)
a black soot streak across the heather and the rock, the heather burnt to
a grey crust and the rock lichen to bare pale stone
a bowl in thin peaty soil over rock, the rim a ring of shattered granite
a heath fire: the heather and bracken black and ash-grey over a wide
patch, the wind-bent trees black, the tors sooted dark

C. Destruction in highland: the impact at three moments (burst, peak, settle). Rock and peat: pale granite chips on long arcs, a brown-grey dust cloud with torn heather in it; a tor sheds blocks that roll downhill.
D. Where it meets its neighbours (hard steps in colour, never a fade; the cover mixes over about a third of the width)
Coastal heath: the sand gives way to heather and bracken on a low cliff, grey
Meadow gives way to moor: heather mounds and bracken among the grass, the first
granite boulders, the ground rising in low humps.
The wood thins to wind-bent trees on heather; granite boulders stand in the
Dry moor: the sand turns to bare weathered rock and thin heather; tors stand on
The crags lower into rounded heath with tors: jagged ridgelines settle into
humps, snow gives way to heather.
Black basalt gives way to pale weathered granite; heather grows in the older,
Spruce stands break up into heather moor; the trees stay in the folds and along
Alpine tundra: lichen and heather mix, boulders and tors stand in the open; snow
An upland bog: peat pools among heather and reed, the ground low and wet between
